Application Materials.content:
Throughout your application you will be given the opportunity to upload scanned documents in support of your application. **A decision on your application may be delayed if the relevant supporting documents are not received.** The following information will usually be needed before a decision can be made on your application:
- Academic reference(s)
- Degree transcripts (interim transcripts)
- English language test certificate (if appropriate)
- Research proposal (if appropriate)
Scanned transcripts and certificates need to be uploaded in the Education section. This page is also where you can upload English language requirement documents. In the Professional/Work experience section, you can upload your CV and detail any relevant work experience that may be beneficial to your application, with space for professional or other qualifications.
Personal statement: approximately **5,000 characters**, explaining why you are interested in studying on your chosen programme. This can be uploaded to the personal statement section in **PDF or Microsoft Word format**, or typed within the application portal. The statement should show interest and commitment to the subject and address: passion for your subject; why you; preparation and evidence of relevant skills; and why Birmingham / why this particular course.
References: you may either upload references if you already have them, or input referee details so the University can contact them after submission. The referee’s contact email address must be an official email address, not a personal one. The University recommends the reference is sent in **PDF format** and, preferably, that it:
- Is on official headed paper with the organisation or university’s logo and address
- Includes the date, your details and the referee’s details
- Summarises how the referee knows you and confirms your suitability for studying on the course
- Is signed by the referee with their official contact details
If you already have a written reference and upload it on behalf of your referee, it must be a scanned copy of the original and on official headed paper. A referee can also email the reference directly to [pgadmissions@contacts.bham.ac.uk](mailto:pgadmissions@contacts.bham.ac.uk) from their official email address, including their full name and role. For the vast majority of programmes, references are not required for a decision to be made; if an offer is made and references are outstanding, they will form part of the offer conditions.
Academic certificate and transcript(s) for all prior degrees: if you have graduated, upload a scan of your original or certified copies of your degree certificate(s) and transcript(s). If you are currently a student, upload an interim transcript from your latest exams. Otherwise your application cannot be considered. You may be asked to send original or certified copies for verification.
Proof of English Language skills: you can scan and upload a copy of your results to the Postgraduate Application Portal. Test results must be no more than two years old from the start date of your course.

Interview Requirements.content: After receiving your application, you may, if you live in the UK, be invited for an interview or to visit the University to discuss your application.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Start date: **September 2026**
- **17 July 2026** Application deadline for international students requiring a visa. We will close applications as soon as the programme is full. Early applications are encouraged.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **2:1 Honours degree or postgraduate diploma** from a UK university or overseas equivalent in **any discipline containing a module with a quantitative element**, such as Business, Economics, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Computer Sciences, Mathematics, Statistics, Science or Commerce.
- Alternatively, **a minimum of GCE A-Level grade B or overseas equivalent in a quantitative subject** may be considered to meet the quantitative requirement.
- Applicants who demonstrate being able to exceed the minimum entry requirements will be given preference.
- For applicants with qualifications from China: students with a **bachelor’s degree (4 years minimum)** may be considered for entry to a postgraduate degree programme, subject to the entry guidance below. MSc Business Analytics is listed under “Economics suite and Non-quantitive programmes” for these China entry requirements.
| Group 院校分组 | PGT entry requirements (2:1 equivalent) / Economics suite and Non-quantitive programmes entry requirement 商学院经济学类和非定量类课程入学要求 |
| --- | --- |
| Group 1 一类大学 | **75%** |
| Group 2 二类大学 | **80%** |
| Group 3 三类大学 | **85%** |
| Group 4 四类大学 | **Reject** |
Applicants undertaking a **3+1 top-up degree** must normally have studied at an approved university in China and graduate from their UK university with a **2:1**. However, for courses taught in Birmingham Business School, applicants undertaking an **SQA Advanced Diploma** may have studied at any Chinese institution if they upload their SQA documents and achieve a **2:1** from their UK university.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If you are an international student, you will need to demonstrate you have a suitable level of English proficiency, usually through the form of an IELTS or equivalent qualification or a Presessional English course. For this course we require **IELTS 6.5 with no less than 6.0 in any band**, which is equivalent to:
- **TOEFL iBT taken before January 2026:** 88 overall with no less than 21 in Reading, 20 Listening, 22 Speaking and 21 in Writing
- **TOEFL iBT taken from January 2026:** 4.5 Overall with no less than 4.5 in any 2 skills and 4 in the other two skills
- **Pearson Test of English (PTE):** Academic 67 with no less than 64 in all four skills
- **Cambridge English: C1 Advanced:** minimum overall score of 176, with no less than 169 in any component
- **LanguageCert ESOL SELT (UKVI):** B2 'Communicator' with no less than 33 in each skill
[View more information](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/taught/apply/international-entry-requirements)
If you have a conditional offer for Birmingham where English is a requirement, you can take a Presessional English course as an alternative to retaking IELTS or a similar qualification. We offer on-campus courses all year round starting from September including additional online courses in the summer term. Teaching takes place in small classes with no more than 18 students to maximise class participation. [Presessional English course](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/subjects/pre-sessional-english-courses/english-for-academic-purposes)

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is delivered in person at Birmingham (Edgbaston), starts in September 2026, lasts 1 year full-time, and awards a Master of Science. The programme is Triple Crown Accredited and ranked Top 70 globally in Business Analytics in the QS Business Masters Rankings 2026.
The MSc Business Analytics programme allows students to gain an understanding of the theory and practice behind business analytics, developing the business understanding, data analytic skills, and ability to communicate insights needed to support informed business decisions. It is suited to those from a variety of backgrounds who are interested in conducting detailed data analysis and translating these insights to resolve practical business issues for organisations from start-ups to global companies.
Programme highlights include:
- Through the Business Analytics Capstone Project, students have the opportunity to gain relevant work experience by analysing a set of data and delivering their findings.
- Students can tailor the programme towards their interests with the Business Analytics micro-courses.
- Students develop the ability to analyse data sets and communicate insights, a skill highly in demand by companies across the globe.
- Birmingham has the largest city economy outside of London with key links to global companies, giving students the opportunity to network with a variety of organisations.
Students have the opportunity to take part in the award-winning Future Leaders Certificate, an extra-curricular programme involving an exciting virtual live project set by a multi-national company. The Future Leaders Certificate helps students understand the impact technology is having on the business world and the implications for their own career.
Birmingham Business School is one of a small number of schools worldwide to hold triple-crown accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA) and the European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS).
Course delivery includes a wide variety of learning and teaching: taught modules including lectures, seminars, tutorials, project and case analysis; assessments including essays and reports, group assessments, presentations and case analysis; and a Capstone Project in which students work in a team to develop a working solution to a live analytics problem. The course comprises 180 credits, taught through a series of 20 credit modules and a 60 credit Capstone Project. As a research-intensive University, teaching is informed by the latest academic thinking and expertise of staff.
Programme Director: [**Robert Fleming**](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/staff/profiles/business/fleming-robert.aspx), Programme Director, MSc Business Analytics. Robert is an experienced programme director with over twenty years' experience.
Career opportunities: This programme allows students to tackle real-world challenges, using data analysis to evaluate the success of previous business projects and forecast future decisions. This skillset is highly in demand by businesses looking to become more efficient and increase growth. The MSc Business Analytics programme is also useful for those who run their own organisations, allowing them to gain an overview of the datasets available and what this means for their business.
Business School students access specialist careers guidance tailored to the global business landscape, including dedicated Business School careers consultants, targeted career coaching, exclusive employer networking events, business-focused careers fairs, direct connections to top graduate recruiters, tailored workshops, one-to-one consultations, and an extensive alumni network. The University is one of the most consistently targeted UK universities by top graduate employers according to the High Fliers report, The Graduate Market 2026.
Student stories include Business Analytics MSc students Gesare Ombati, Hazel, Jawad Zaarif, and Shafkat Rahman, and Business Analytics alumni Poojan Pavagadhi.

Cost of Attendance.content:
- **Living expenses:** Postgraduate students who opt to live in halls of residence will require **£15,192** and those who opt to rent privately will require **£12,688** to cover their expenses for food and housing over a 52 week period.
- **Miscellaneous personal expenses:** An allowance of **£80 per week** if living in halls or **£114 per week** if renting privately. For postgraduate students this is calculated over 52 weeks: **£4,160** if living in halls and **£5,928** if renting privately. These expenses include utilities, clothing, leisure and cell phone.
- **Books, course materials, supplies and equipment:** **£1,000** for each year of study.
- **PC/Laptop:** **£900** in Year 1, **£300** for each subsequent year of study for maintenance.
- **Transportation:** This includes a set cost of **£2,000** for two return flights from the USA to the UK and local transportation of **£1,508** for postgraduate students.
- **IHS Surcharge/Visa Fee:** For a full time postgraduate taught student on a one year programme, Visa Fees are **£524** and Immigration Health Surcharge is **£1,164**.

Financial Aid.content:
To help you afford your studies, Birmingham has put more than £33 million into student support and scholarships and offers advice on searching for funding and managing your finances. [Explore scholarships and funding](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/taught/fees-funding)
Birmingham Business School Masters Scholarships are designed to empower the next generation of leaders who are passionate about advancing responsible business and driving positive change. For 2026, Birmingham Business School is offering several scholarships to invest in future leaders who will set new global standards for responsible business leadership through challenging the status quo to seek progressive solutions to complex global challenges. [Find out more](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/schools/business/courses/masters/scholarships)
For international students, Birmingham has made more than £10.5 million in scholarships available for international students coming to study at Birmingham. [Discover international scholarships](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/international/fees/scholarships)

Multiple Applications.content: Your application is specifically designed for the programme you have applied for via your course page. You can apply to more than one Masters course but each personal statement should be slightly different so that it is relevant to the individual course.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
If you are unable to attend the programme for the academic year specified in your offer letter, please inform the Admissions Office: contact details are stated in your offer letter. If you wish to defer for more than **one year**, you will need to submit a new application.
International students issued an offer to study a taught postgraduate programme are required to pay a non-refundable tuition fee deposit of **£2,000** to secure their place. The deposit payment will be deducted from the tuition fee at registration. [Deposit policy information](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/university/colleges/professional/external/admissions/deposit-refund-policy-pgt.aspx "deposit policy")

Conditional Admission Policy.content: If you have a conditional offer for Birmingham where English is a requirement, you can take a [Presessional English course](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/subjects/pre-sessional-english-courses/english-for-academic-purposes) as an alternative to retaking IELTS or a similar qualification. The University offers on-campus courses all year round starting from September, including additional online courses in the summer term.
